description: Voluntary Provident Fund under EPF Scheme para 26(6): the MEMBER may contribute above the statutory 12%, and the employer is under NO obligation to match it — para 26(6) requires a separate agreement for a matching contribution. The employer here has also restricted itself to the ceiling under para 26A(2). Hand derivation: statutory wage 40000.0000, base CEILING -> statutory base 15000.0000, no above-ceiling excess, EPF/EPS/EDLI wages 15000.0000; employee statutory 12% of 15000.0000 = 1800; the employee elected a VOLUNTARY base of 25000.0000, so the VPF is 12% of 25000.0000 = 3000 and the employee's total deduction is 4800, which is well under the 50% of wages cap in s.18(2) of the Code on Wages 2019; the employer contributes NOTHING on the voluntary base, so its EPS stays 1250 and its EPF share stays 550.

counterfactual.why: If the engine ignored the para 26A(2) restriction and the para 26(6) proviso — computing on ACTUAL wages with the employer matching the VPF — the employer's EPF share would be 6550 instead of 550 and the employee's deduction 7800 instead of 4800. The company would over-remit 6000 every month and the employee would be short-paid 3000.
